summary: @onereach/orest-jest-presets ships obfuscated preinstall dropper that downloads Bun runtime and executes opaque bundle
details: The package declares itself as Jest presets but its package.json preinstall hook runs setup.mjs, an obfuscator.io-style launcher (hex-prefixed identifiers, per-function string-lookup indirection) whose only purpose is to locate or download the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases and execute the bundled sibling file math_init.js under it. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-precompiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) using string-array rotation obfuscation (function WV8StW shifting a large numeric/string table), so its runtime behavior is not inspectable from source. A Jest preset package has no legitimate need for an alternate language runtime or an opaque compiled payload executed at npm install time. The obfuscation of both the launcher and the executed bundle, combined with the purpose mismatch and automatic execution via the preinstall lifecycle hook, matches the alternate-runtime dropper attack pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
